top_signals.title: SEC Warns Activist Investors After Climate Push at Exxon Mobil
top_signals.summary: The US Securities and Exchange Commission warned asset managers and activist investors about their reporting obligations following a shareholder campaign in 2021 to remove Exxon Mobil Corp. directors over their record on climate.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Unpacking the M&A Slowdown
top_signals.summary:
M&A deal values are slipping as uncertainty rises around elections, rates, and regulation. Paul Aversano,  Global Practice Leader of Global Transaction Advisory Group at Alvarez & Marsal, joins Bloomberg Open Interest to explain why large, debt-heavy buyouts are feeling the most pressure, how mid-market deals are holding up, and where global hotspots and AI-driven risks are emerging.

Correction: "This video was edited to correct the spelling of "Paul Aversano" that aired in the program at 10:10 am ET." (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Inflation expectations impacting rate path, bonds and global risk assets.

top_signals.title: Crypto card access doesn’t match global demand, Tangem says
top_signals.summary: Crypto card demand can be stronger where access is harder, Tangem says, as it expands its Visa payment offering, allowing users to spend from its self-custodial wallet.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Digital asset volatility and institutional crypto positioning changes.

top_signals.title: Citi Says Private Equity Hasn’t Slowed Poaching of Bankers
top_signals.summary: David Friedland, co-head of North America investment banking at Citi, says private equity firms are still aggressively poaching young bankers from Wall Street banks. He talks about Citi’s plan to accelerate promotions and provide higher pay to its junior bankers. (Source: Bloomberg)
